units.literal: Lady Xun pled before Colonel Director of Retainers He Zeng, begging to become an official bondmaid to redeem Zhi’s life.

units.zh: 曾哀之，使主簿程咸上議曰：「夫司寇作典，建三等之制；
units.en: He Zeng grieved over this and had his Registrar Cheng Xian submit a deliberation, saying, "When the Minister of Crime made the canon, he established the system of three grades;
units.literal: He Zeng grieved over this and had his Registrar Cheng Xian submit a deliberation, saying, "When the Minister of Crime made the canon, he established the system of three grades;

units.zh: 甫侯修刑，通輕重之法。
units.en: Fu marquis tuned statutes linking lighter and graver penalties.
units.literal: Marquis Fu polished punishments, threading light and heavy sentences.

units.zh: 叔世多變，秦立重辟，漢又修之。
units.en: Every dynasty reworked Qin-Han severity.
units.literal: Late ages shifted endlessly—Qin devised cruel executions; Han piled more atop.

units.zh: 大魏承秦漢之弊，未及革制，所以追戮已出之女，誠欲殄丑類之族也。
units.en: Wei still copied harsh collateral rules to stamp out traitorous houses.
units.literal: Great Wei inherited Qin-Han abuses before systemic overhaul—so tracing punishment to married-away daughters aimed to exterminate villainous kin.

units.zh: 然則法貴得中，刑慎過制。
units.en: Still, statute must stay balanced—never overshoot.
units.literal: Yet law prizes proportionality; punishments must fear crossing limits.

units.zh: 臣以為女人有三從之義，無自專之道，出適他族，還喪父母，降其服紀，所以明外成之節，異在室之恩。
units.en: Women follow father, husband, son—rites distinguish maidens from wives.
units.literal: Your servant believes women observe three obediences and lack independent agency; married into another surname and returning to mourn parents they lower mourning grades—thereby marking outsider ritual boundaries distinct from daughters still unmarried.

units.zh: 而父母有罪，追刑已出之女；
units.en: Parents’ guilt nevertheless dragged married daughters back under the blade.
units.literal: Yet when parents sin, punishment pursues daughters already married away;

units.zh: 夫黨見誅，又有隨姓之戮。
units.en: If husbands’ clans fell, wives died twice over.
units.literal: When husband’s faction is executed they again suffer surname-linked slaughter.

units.zh: 一人之身，內外受辟。
units.en: A single woman answered both natal and marital guilt.
units.literal: One body suffers executions from both inner and outer kin.

units.zh: 今女既嫁，則為異姓之妻；
units.en: Marriage transfers loyalty to the husband’s house.
units.literal: Once wed she belongs to another surname’s wife;

units.zh: 如或產育，則為他族之母，此為元惡之所忽。
units.en: Motherhood anchors her with her children’s clan—tyrants ignored this.
units.literal: If she bears sons she becomes mother to another lineage—points vicious regimes overlook.

units.zh: 戮無辜之所重，於防則不足懲奸亂之源，於情則傷孝子之心。
units.en: Executing guiltless women neither stops rebellion nor consoles loyal sons.
units.literal: Slaughtering innocents weighs heavily: deterrence cannot plug treason’s spring yet sentiment wounds filial sons.

units.zh: 男不得罪於他族，而女獨嬰戮於二門，非所以哀矜女弱，蠲明法制之本分也。
units.en: Men escaped cross-clan guilt while women died twice—hardly mercy or clarity.
units.literal: Men incur no guilt from alien clans yet women alone endure blades from two gates—not how to pity frail wives or clarify law’s core divisions.

units.zh: 臣以為在室之女，從父母之誅；
units.en: Unmarried daughters share parental punishment.
units.literal: Your servant proposes daughters still at home follow parental sentences;

units.zh: 既醮之婦，從夫家之罰。
units.en: Wives answer husband-house crimes alone.
units.literal: Women who have drunk nuptial wine follow husband-house penalties.

units.zh: 宜改舊科，以為永制。」
units.en: The old statutes should be changed, and this should be made an enduring system."
units.literal: The old statutes should be changed, and this should be made an enduring system."

units.zh: 於是有詔改定律令。
units.en: An imperial order rewrote the law accordingly.
units.literal: Thereupon an edict revised statutes and commands.

units.zh: 文帝為晉王，患前代律令本注煩雜，陳群、劉邵雖經改革，而科網本密，又叔孫、郭、馬、杜諸儒章句，但取鄭氏，又為偏黨，未可承用。
units.en: When Emperor Wen was King of Jin, he was troubled that the statutes and ordinances, root texts and notes of earlier generations were complicated and miscellaneous. Although Chen Qun and Liu Shao had revised them, the statutory net was basically dense, and the chapter-and-verse commentaries of Shusun, Guo, Ma, Du, and other classicists took only Zheng Xuan's school and were also partial and partisan, so they could not be adopted.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen was King of Jin, he was troubled that the statutes and ordinances, root texts and notes of earlier generations were complicated and miscellaneous. Although Chen Qun and Liu Shao had revised them, the statutory net was basically dense, and the chapter-and-verse commentaries of Shusun, Guo, Ma, Du, and other classicists took only Zheng Xuan's school and were also partial and partisan, so they could not be adopted.

units.zh: 於是令賈充定法律，令與太傅鄭沖、司徒荀顗、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜、中護軍王業、廷尉杜友、守河南尹杜預、散騎侍郎裴楷、潁川太守周雄、齊相郭頎、騎都尉成公綏、尚書郎柳軌及吏部令史榮邵等十四人典其事，就漢九章增十一篇，仍其族類，正其體號，改舊律為《刑名》、《法例》，辨《囚律》為《告劾》、《系訊》、《斷獄》，分《盜律》為《請賕》、《詐偽》、《水火》、《毀亡》，因事類為《衛宮》、《違制》，撰《周官》為《諸侯律》，合二十篇，六百二十條，二萬七千六百五十七言。
units.en: He therefore ordered Jia Chong to settle the laws and statutes, and ordered him together with Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Minister over the Masses Xun Yi, Palace Writer Director Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, Central Protector of the Army Wang Ye, Commandant of Justice Du You, Acting Governor of Henan Du Yu, Cavalier Attendant Pei Kai, Yingchuan Grand Administrator Zhou Xiong, Qi Chancellor Guo Qi, Cavalier Commandant Chenggong Sui, Secretariat Gentleman Liu Gui, Personnel Bureau Clerk Rong Shao, and the others, fourteen men in all, to manage the affair. Based on the Han Nine Chapters, they added eleven chapters, followed their categories, corrected their structures and titles, changed the old code into Penal Names and Legal Precedents, divided the Prisoners Code into Accusations and Impeachments, Detentions and Interrogations, and Deciding Prison Cases, divided the Robbery Code into Requests and Bribes, Fraud and Forgery, Water and Fire, and Destruction and Loss, made Palace Guards and Violations of Regulations according to the categories of affairs, and compiled the Zhou Offices into the Feudal Lords Code. Together these made twenty chapters, six hundred and twenty articles, and twenty-seven thousand six hundred fifty-seven words.
units.literal: He therefore ordered Jia Chong to settle the laws and statutes, and ordered him together with Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Minister over the Masses Xun Yi, Palace Writer Director Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, Central Protector of the Army Wang Ye, Commandant of Justice Du You, Acting Governor of Henan Du Yu, Cavalier Attendant Pei Kai, Yingchuan Grand Administrator Zhou Xiong, Qi Chancellor Guo Qi, Cavalier Commandant Chenggong Sui, Secretariat Gentleman Liu Gui, Personnel Bureau Clerk Rong Shao, and the others, fourteen men in all, to manage the affair. Based on the Han Nine Chapters, they added eleven chapters, followed their categories, corrected their structures and titles, changed the old code into Penal Names and Legal Precedents, divided the Prisoners Code into Accusations and Impeachments, Detentions and Interrogations, and Deciding Prison Cases, divided the Robbery Code into Requests and Bribes, Fraud and Forgery, Water and Fire, and Destruction and Loss, made Palace Guards and Violations of Regulations according to the categories of affairs, and compiled the Zhou Offices into the Feudal Lords Code. Together these made twenty chapters, six hundred and twenty articles, and twenty-seven thousand six hundred fifty-seven words.

units.zh: 蠲其苛穢，存其清約，事從中典，歸於益時。
units.en: Editors stripped cruft, kept crisp rules, and tuned everything to contemporary needs.
units.literal: They cut filth and kept essentials—matters follow central canons and aim to benefit the age.

units.zh: 其餘未宜除者，若軍事、田農、酤酒，未得皆從人心，權設其法，太平當除，故不入律，悉以為令。
units.en: Military, agrarian, and liquor rules stayed provisional edicts until a future peaceful reign could prune them.
units.literal: Matters not yet fit for repeal—such as military affairs, farming, or liquor monopolies—could not all follow popular wishes; they provisionally set laws to be repealed in Great Peace, therefore not embedded in statutes but collected as edicts.

units.zh: 施行制度，以此設教，違令有罪則入律。
units.en: Administrative handbooks taught policy; breaching those edicts triggered codified penalties.
units.literal: Institutions implementing policy used these for instruction—violating edicts became statutory crime.

units.zh: 其常事品式章程，各還其府，為故事。
units.en: Everyday paperwork stayed departmental precedent rather than criminal code.
units.literal: Routine administrative forms and memorial templates returned to their bureaus as precedent dossiers.

units.zh: 減梟斬族誅從坐之條，除謀反適養母出女嫁皆不復還坐父母棄市，省禁固相告之條，去捕亡、亡沒為官奴婢之制。
units.en: Penal reform softened exposure executions, limited clan guilt for treason and adoption cases, scrapped denunciation prisons, and ended fugitive enslavement rules.
units.literal: They reduced provisions on displaying heads, waist-cutting, clan execution, and accessory sitting; removed returning parents to marketplace execution for treason, adopted heirs, divorced daughters; dropped mutual denunciation imprisonment; abolished arrest fugitive statutes and enslavement of fugitives’ kin.

units.zh: 輕過誤老少女人當罰金杖罰者，皆令半之。
units.en: Fines and beatings for minors, seniors, women, and petty slips were automatically cut in half.
units.literal: Light offenses, mistakes, old age, youth, or women liable for cash or cane had sentences halved.

units.zh: 重奸伯叔母之令，棄市。
units.en: Incest with uncles or aunts now meant immediate public execution.
units.literal: They strengthened the statute on violating paternal uncles and aunts—marketplace execution.

units.zh: 淫寡女，三歲刑。
units.en: Seducing bereaved women earned three years penal labor.
units.literal: Fornicating with widows brought three years labor.

units.zh: 崇嫁娶之要，一以下娉為正，不理私約。
units.en: Marriage validity rested solely on documented bride-price, not secret promises.
units.literal: They elevated marriage essentials—only formal betrothal gifts counted; private pledges were ignored.

units.zh: 峻禮教之防，准五服以制罪也。
units.en: Law enforced mourning hierarchies when calibrating criminal guilt.
units.literal: They fortified ritual barriers and matched punishments to the five mourning grades.

units.zh: 凡律令合二千九百二十六條，十二萬六千三百言，六十卷，故事三十卷。
units.en: The codex stacked 2,926 provisions across sixty volumes plus thirty precedent fascicles.
units.literal: Statutes and edicts together numbered 2,926 articles, 126,300 characters, sixty scrolls; precedent dossiers thirty scrolls.

units.zh: 泰始三年，事畢，表上。
units.en: In the third year of Taishi, the completed code was presented to the throne.
units.literal: In Taishi third year the work finished and they memorialized it upward.

units.zh: 武帝詔曰：「昔蕭何以定律令受封，叔孫通制儀為奉常，賜金五百斤，弟子百人皆為郎。
units.en: Emperor Wu issued an edict, saying, "Formerly Xiao He received an enfeoffment for settling statutes and ordinances, and Shusun Tong made ritual regulations, became Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was granted five hundred jin of gold, and one hundred of his disciples all became gentlemen.
units.literal: Emperor Wu issued an edict, saying, "Formerly Xiao He received an enfeoffment for settling statutes and ordinances, and Shusun Tong made ritual regulations, became Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was granted five hundred jin of gold, and one hundred of his disciples all became gentlemen.

units.zh: 夫立功立事，古今之所重，宜加祿賞，其詳考差敘。
units.en: Reward the compilers commensurate with their service.
units.literal: Establishing merit has always mattered—add salaries and rewards; investigate ranks carefully.

units.zh: 輒如詔簡異弟子百人，隨才品用，賞帛萬餘匹。」
units.en: At once, according to the edict, one hundred exceptional disciples were selected, employed according to their talents and grades, and rewarded with more than ten thousand bolts of silk."
units.literal: At once, according to the edict, one hundred exceptional disciples were selected, employed according to their talents and grades, and rewarded with more than ten thousand bolts of silk."

units.zh: 武帝親自臨講，使裴楷執讀。
units.en: Wudi presided while Pei Kai recited the new code.
units.literal: Emperor Wu personally attended the lecture and had Pei Kai read aloud.

units.zh: 四年正月，大赦天下，乃班新律。
units.en: In the first month of year four he amnestied the realm and published the Jin code.
units.literal: Fourth year, first month, he proclaimed a general amnesty and promulgated the new statutes.

units.zh: 其後，明法掾張裴又注律，表上之，其要曰：
units.en: Zhang Pei’s statutory commentary begins:
units.literal: Later legal clerk Zhang Pei annotated the statutes, memorialized them, summarizing:

units.zh: 律始於《刑名》者，所以定罪制也；
units.en: Punishment Names opens the code because it defines offense labels and scales.
units.literal: Statutes open with Punishment Names because that fascicle fixes guilt and measures.

units.zh: 終於《諸侯》者，所以畢其政也。
units.en: Feudal Lords closes the book because it finishes jurisdictional rules.
units.literal: They end with Feudal Lords because that fascicle completes governance.

units.zh: 王政布于上，諸侯奉于下，禮樂撫於中，故有三才之義焉，其相須而成，若一體焉。
units.en: Editorial structure mirrors heaven-earth-man coordination across statutes.
units.literal: Royal policy spreads above, feudal lords obey below, ritual and music soothe within—thus the triad of heaven, earth, and man mutually completes like one body.

units.zh: 《刑名》所以經略罪法之輕重，正加減之等差，明發眾篇之多義，補其章條之不足，較舉上下綱領。
units.en: The opening fascicle harmonizes sentencing ladders across the entire code.
units.literal: Punishment Names sets out the relative severity of offenses, corrects the gradations of increase and reduction, clarifies the many meanings of the other chapters, supplements insufficient articles, and aligns their overarching principles.

units.zh: 其犯盜賊、詐偽、請賕者，則求罪於此，作役、水火、畜養、守備之細事，皆求之作本名。
units.en: Core crimes resolve through Names while petty administrative offenses cite their titled chapters.
units.literal: Robbery, fraud, and bribery seek guilt definitions here; corvée labor, fire and water, livestock, guard duties seek native fascicle titles.

units.zh: 告訊為之心舌，捕系為之手足，斷獄為之定罪，名例齊其制。
units.en: Litigation flows tongue-to-hand-to-verdict under unified principles.
units.literal: Accusation and interrogation serve as tongue; arrest and binding as limbs; trial verdicts fix guilt—general principles knit the system.

units.zh: 自始及終，往而不窮，變動無常，周流四極，上下無方，不離於法律之中也。
units.en: Flexible doctrine stays anchored despite exhaustive hypotheticals.
units.literal: From beginning to end movement never exhausts; changes lack fixity; it circles four extremes and rises or sinks without fixed direction—yet never departs from legal order.

units.zh: 其知而犯之謂之故，意以為然謂之失，違忠欺上謂之謾，背信藏巧謂之詐，虧禮廢節謂之不敬，兩訟相趣謂之鬥，兩和相害謂之戲，無變斬擊謂之賊，不意誤犯謂之過失，逆節絕理謂之不道，陵上僭貴謂之惡逆，將害未發謂之戕，唱首先言謂之造意，二人對議謂之謀，制眾建計謂之率，不和謂之強，攻惡謂之略，三人謂之群，取非其物謂之盜，貨財之利謂之贓：凡二十者，律義之較名也。
units.en: Zhang Pei lists twenty definitional contrasts—intent versus negligence, fraud versus jest—that judges use like diagnostic labels.
units.literal: Knowing yet offending is called intentional; believing it correct is called negligent fault; betraying loyalty and deceiving superiors is called deceit; breaking faith and hiding craft is called fraud; violating ritual propriety is called irreverence; two lawsuits rushing together is called affray; mutual consent harming is called horseplay; unchanged hacking blows are called banditry; unintentional mistake is called accidental fault; opposing cosmic order is called lack of the Way; bullying superiors and usurping honor is called monstrous rebellion; intending harm not yet launched is called plotted assault; first voicing a scheme is called initiating intent; two plotting together is called conspiracy; directing masses plotting is called leading; unwilling coercion is called forced assault; seizing evil opportunity is called raid; three conspirators is called gang; taking goods not one’s own is called theft; profiting goods is called embezzlement—in all twenty items defining comparative statutory labels.

units.zh: 夫律者，當慎其變，審其理。
units.en: Good adjudication tracks shifting facts and moral nuance.
units.literal: Statutes must heed transformations and examine rationales.

units.zh: 若不承用詔書，無故失之刑，當從贖。
units.en: Ignorant mishandling of imperial orders qualifies for redeemable fines.
units.literal: When someone fails to apply edict letters without cause the negligence punishment ought to follow redemption.

units.zh: 謀反之同伍，實不知情，當從刑。
units.en: Five-house rebel neighbors bear graded punishment even if ignorant—a deliberate severity.
units.literal: Neighbors of rebels who truly knew nothing ought nonetheless face statutory punishment.

units.zh: 此故失之變也。
units.en: Such edge cases refine intent doctrine.
units.literal: These illustrate transformations between intentional and negligent fault.

units.zh: 卑與尊鬥，皆為賊。
units.en: Any status mix in brawls triggers bandit-law scrutiny.
units.literal: When inferior and superior fight both count as banditry.

units.zh: 鬥之加兵刃水火中，不得為戲，戲之重也。
units.en: Introducing lethal tools upgrades jest to assault.
units.literal: If fight introduces blades fire or water mid-struggle it cannot be horseplay—horseplay’s gravity differs.

units.zh: 向人室廬道徑射，不得為過，失之禁也。
units.en: Reckless shooting near dwellings breaks absolute bans regardless of intent.
units.literal: Shooting toward residences paths cannot count as accident—the prohibition covers inadvertence.

units.zh: 都城人眾中走馬殺人，當為賊，賊之似也。
units.en: Fatal stampedes in royal cities mimic malicious killing.
units.literal: Galloping horses through crowded capital streets killing people counts as banditry—akin to predatory crime.

units.zh: 過失似賊，戲似鬥，鬥而殺傷傍人，又似誤，盜傷縛守似強盜，呵人取財似受賕，囚辭所連似告劾，諸勿聽理似故縱，持質似恐猲。
units.en: Zhang Pei catalogs mimetic offenses requiring careful discrimination.
units.literal: Accidental injury resembling banditry, horseplay resembling affray, affray injuring bystanders resembling mistake, thieves injuring bound guards resembling robbery, berating people for property resembling bribery, prisoner statements chaining others resembling accusation, ignoring hearings resembling connivance, hostage-taking resembling terror—all blur categories.

units.zh: 如此之比，皆為無常之格也。
units.en: Judges rely on these sliding scales when labels collide.
units.literal: Patterns such as these constitute fluid comparative grids.

units.zh: 五刑不簡，正於五罰，五罰不服，正於五過，意善功惡，以金贖之。
units.en: Classical five-fine ladder fills gaps when corporal punishment misfires.
units.literal: When five punishments resist simplification rectify with five fines; when fines resist obey five excess judgments—good intent yet bad outcome redeems with metal.

units.zh: 故律制，生罪不過十四等，死刑不過三，徒加不過六，囚加不過五，累作不過十一歲，累笞不過千二百，刑等不過一歲，金等不過四兩。
units.en: The code therefore caps gradations at every step: no more than fourteen living-crime ranks, three capital grades, six labor enhancements, five detention enhancements, eleven cumulative labor years, twelve hundred cumulative strokes, one-year sentence increments, and four-tael cash increments.
units.literal: Thus statutes cap living offenses at fourteen grades, capital at three, labor aggravation at six, imprisonment aggravation at five, cumulative labor not beyond eleven years, cumulative flogging not beyond 1,200 strokes, sentence increments within one year, cash increments within four taels.

units.zh: 月贖不計日，日作不拘月，歲數不疑閏。
units.en: Sentence accounting ignores fractional moons or leap months.
units.literal: Monthly redemption ignores partial days; daily labor ignores calendar months; yearly counts ignore intercalary months.

units.zh: 不以加至死，並死不復加。
units.en: Capital punishment caps aggravation ladders.
units.literal: Aggravation never stacks to death; combined death cannot stack further.

units.zh: 不可累者，故有並數；
units.en: Some bans run concurrently rather than sequentially.
units.literal: What cannot accumulate therefore uses parallel numbering;

units.zh: 不可並數，乃累其加。
units.en: Other offenses aggregate aggravation instead.
units.literal: what cannot run parallel then stacks increments.

units.zh: 以加論者，但得其加；
units.en: Aggravation sentencing isolates the marginal penalty.
units.literal: When judging by aggravation capture only the aggravating increment;

units.zh: 與加同者，連得其本。
units.en: Matching tiers revert to baseline guilt.
units.literal: when identical with aggravation link back to base offense.

units.zh: 不在次者，不以通論。
units.en: Off-sequence crimes resist unified analogy.
units.literal: When outside sequence do not blend doctrines.

units.zh: 以人得罪與人同，以法得罪與法同。
units.en: Personal versus procedural guilt follow distinct tracks.
units.literal: Personal guilt aligns with persons; statutory guilt aligns with statutes.

units.zh: 侵生害死，不可齊其防；
units.en: Harm to corpses versus persons demands different shields.
units.literal: Injuring the living versus harming the dead cannot share identical defenses;

units.zh: 親疏公私，不可常其教。
units.en: Public versus familial crimes need tailored instruction.
units.literal: Kinship distance and public versus private cannot fix one universal teaching.

units.zh: 禮樂崇於上，故降其刑；
units.en: Higher ritual standing earns lighter penalties.
units.literal: Because ritual and music are lofty above punishments lighten;

units.zh: 刑法閑于下，故全其法。
units.en: Lower strata rely on exhaustive statute to preserve full protection.
units.literal: because punishments operate below the statutes preserve completeness.

units.zh: 是故尊卑敘，仁義明，九族親，王道平也。
units.en: Balanced gradations yield humane clarity across kin networks.
units.literal: Therefore noble and base order themselves; benevolence and righteousness clarify; nine kinship circles harmonize; kingly way levels.

units.zh: 律有事狀相似而罪名相涉者，若加威勢下手取財為強盜，不自知亡為縛守，將中有惡言為恐猲，不以罪名呵為呵人，以罪名呵為受賕，劫召其財為持質。
units.en: Six intimidation economies share coercion yet earn distinct labels—robbery, jailbreak assistance, terror, shakedown, bribery, hostage seizure.
units.literal: Statutes contain fact-patterns resembling each other yet implicating different crimes—using intimidation to seize property is robbery; unknowingly guarding escapees is custodial binding; threatening with wicked words is terror extortion; berating without naming crime is verbal seizure; berating with named crime is bribery; seizing property by coercion is hostage-taking.

units.zh: 此六者，以威勢得財而名殊者也。
units.en: Same coercive profit stream splits across six statutory names.
units.literal: These six gain wealth through awe though titles differ.

units.zh: 即不求自與為受求，所監求而後取為盜贓，輸入呵受為留難，斂人財物積藏於官為擅賦，加歐擊之為戮辱。
units.en: Solicitation, supervised theft, bureaucratic obstruction, and illegal surcharges each refine bribery’s shades.
units.literal: Not requesting yet accepting is soliciting bribes; supervisors demanding then taking is embezzled theft; funneling seized goods through authorities is obstruction; stockpiling levies inside offices is unauthorized taxation; superimposed beatings become humiliating injury.

units.zh: 諸如此類，皆為以威勢得財而罪相似者也。
units.en: Wealth-by-intimidation cases remain cognate despite label shifts.
units.literal: All such cases share coercive enrichment with similar guilt.

units.zh: 夫刑者，司理之官；
units.en: Criminal law administers underlying pattern.
units.literal: Punishment is the office of managing principle;

units.zh: 理者，求情之機，情者，心神之使。
units.en: Legal reasoning traces outward facts to inward intent.
units.literal: Principle is the trigger for seeking facts; facts are the envoys of mind and spirit.

units.zh: 心感則情動於中，而形於言？
units.en: Does not emotion voice itself outward once the heart stirs?
units.literal: When the mind stirs, emotion moves within and takes form in words?

units.zh: 暢于四支，發於事業。
units.en: It flows through the four limbs and finds expression in every deed.
units.literal: It extends through the four limbs and emerges in affairs.

units.zh: 是故奸人心愧而面赤，內怖而色奪。
units.en: Villains blanch or flush when truth closes in.
units.literal: Therefore wicked people inwardly shame yet flush red, inwardly fear yet lose color.

units.zh: 論罪者務本其心，審其情，精其事，近取諸身，遠取諸物，然後乃可以正刑。
units.en: Judges must triangulate motive, fact, and physical tells before sentencing.
units.literal: Sentencers must root in mind, examine facts, refine incidents, take evidence from the body, seek analogies in things—only then can punishment be just.

units.zh: 仰手似乞，俯手似奪，捧手似謝，擬手似訴，拱臂似自首，攘臂似格鬥，矜莊似威，怡悅似福，喜怒憂歡，貌在聲色。
units.en: Zhang Pei lists gesture and expression lexicons for inferring intent.
units.literal: Upturned hands resemble begging; downturned hands resemble seizing; cupped hands resemble thanks; imitative hands resemble pleading; folded arms resemble surrender; flung arms resemble brawl; composed bearing resembles awe; glad faces resemble blessing; joy, anger, grief, pleasure sit in voice and countenance.

units.zh: 奸真猛弱，候在視息。
units.en: Breathing tempo and eye flicker betray truth.
units.literal: Cunning or honesty, violence or weakness—await breath and glance.

units.zh: 出口有言當為告，下手有禁當為賊，喜子殺怒子當為戲，怒子殺喜子當為賊。
units.en: Voice versus fist distinguishes accusation from assault; mood contrasts redefine jest versus malice.
units.literal: Speech exiting constitutes accusation; forbidden blows descending constitute banditry; joyful son killing angry son counts as horseplay; angry son killing joyful son counts as banditry.

units.zh: 諸如此類，自非至精不能極其理也。
units.en: Only meticulous inference clarifies such overlaps.
units.literal: Analogies such as these demand utmost refinement or principle stays obscure.

units.zh: 律之名例，非正文而分明也。
units.en: General Part doctrines illuminate without occupying numbered articles.
units.literal: Statutory general principles are not main-text clauses yet remain luminous.

units.zh: 若八十，非殺傷人，他皆勿論，即誣告謀反者反坐。
units.en: Octogenarians skip liability except for homicide, while false accusers of treason face reverse judgment.
units.literal: If age eighty, except for killing or wounding another, all else goes undiscussed; false accusers of plotting rebellion sit reversed.

units.zh: 十歲，不得告言人；
units.en: Children under ten cannot file suit.
units.literal: At age ten one may not accuse others in court.

units.zh: 即奴婢捍主，主得謁殺之。
units.en: When slaves resist masters, the master may petition to kill them.
units.literal: If bond servants strike masters, the master may report and execute them.

units.zh: 賊燔人廬舍積聚，盜贓五匹以上，棄市；
units.en: Arson and major theft above five bolts drew public execution.
units.literal: Bandits who burn houses or storehouses, or steal five bolts of goods or more, face marketplace execution.

units.zh: 即燔官府積聚盜，亦當與同。
units.en: Official granaries burned or robbed faced identical sanctions.
units.literal: If burning official storehouses or stealing there, treat the same.

units.zh: 歐人教令者與同罪，即令人歐其父母，不可與行者同得重也。
units.en: Instigating assault tracks accomplice liability; ordering parental assault differs from acting.
units.literal: Those who instruct beatings share the striker's guilt; ordering someone to beat parents cannot receive the same heavy sentence as the striker.

units.zh: 若得遺物強取強乞之類，無還贓法隨例畀之文。
units.en: Forced recovery of lost goods uses precedent restitution clauses.
units.literal: If forcibly taking lost property or begging by force—when no restitution statute exists—follow exemplar rules on surrender.

units.zh: 法律中諸不敬，違儀失式，及犯罪為公為私，贓入身不入身，皆隨事輕重取法，以例求其名也。
units.en: Statutory taxonomy sorts ritual faults, public/private guilt, and tangible versus intangible spoils by degrees.
units.literal: Within statutes every category of irreverence, ritual lapse, public versus private crime, embezzlement entering person or coffers—each follows incident severity to retrieve the proper label.

units.zh: 夫理者，精玄之妙，不可以一方行也；
units.en: Legal principle refuses single-track formulas.
units.literal: Principle is subtle mystery—it cannot travel on one track.

units.zh: 律者，幽理之奧，不可以一體守也。
units.en: Written law cannot freeze into one rigid mold.
units.literal: Statute is abstruse principle—it cannot be guarded as one rigid body.

units.zh: 或計過以配罪，或化略以循常，或隨事以盡情，或趣舍以從時，或推重以立防，或引輕而就下。
units.en: Judges weigh fault-matching, simplified defaults, fact-sensitive mercy, seasonal policy shifts, harsh deterrence, or lenient relief.
units.literal: Sometimes match fault to crime, sometimes simplify outline to follow norms, sometimes exhaust sentiment with facts, sometimes advance or retreat with seasons, sometimes erect heavy fences, sometimes draw light toward leniency.

units.zh: 公私廢避之宜，除削重輕之變，皆所以臨時觀釁，使用法執詮者幽於未制之中，采其根牙之微，致之於機格之上，稱輕重於豪銖，考輩類于參伍，然後乃可以理直刑正。
units.en: Elastic doctrines let judges weigh mitigations, scan microscopic facts, and align sentences through layered analogy.
units.literal: Matters of avoiding public or private duty, cutting or amplifying severity—all rely on watching cracks in the moment so jurists holding glossaries probe unreached scenarios, capture root tendrils, raise them to procedural frameworks, balance weight on fine scales, compare kinds in five-fold arrays—only then can principle straighten and punishments align.

units.zh: 夫奉聖典者若操刀執繩，刀妄加則傷物，繩妄彈則侵直。
units.en: Judges wield law like blade and plumb-line—careless use mis-harms.
units.literal: Those wielding sacred canons are like holding knife or cord—misapplied knife wounds creatures, mis-snapped cord wrongs the straight.

units.zh: 梟首者惡之長，斬刑者罪之大，棄市者死之下，髡作者刑之威，贖罰者誤之誡。
units.en: Five punishments grade horror from head-display to fines.
units.literal: Displaying heads crowns villainy; waist-cutting marks greatest guilt; marketplace execution ranks lowest death; shaved labor shows penal awe; redemption warns negligence.

units.zh: 王者立此五刑，所以寶君子而逼小人，故為敕慎之經，皆擬《周易》有變通之體焉。
units.en: Royal punishments elevate virtue while intimidating vice, modeled on Change's flexibility.
units.literal: The king institutes these five punishments to treasure gentlemen and press petty men—therefore canonical caution threads through them, each patterned on Zhou Changes' adaptive mode.

units.zh: 欲令提綱而大道清，舉略而王法齊，其旨遠，其辭文，其言曲而中，其事肆而隱。
units.en: Sparse wording masks vast regulatory intent.
units.literal: They intend that lifting the net clears the great Way; raising the outline aligns kingly law—intent remote, rhetoric ornate, words bent yet hitting center, affairs expansive yet hidden.

units.zh: 通天下之志唯忠也，斷天下之疑唯文也，切天下之情唯遠也，彌天下之務唯大也，變無常體唯理也，非天下之賢聖，孰能與於斯！
units.en: Only canonical virtues decode law's cosmic scope.
units.literal: Only loyalty penetrates all wills under heaven; only pattern cuts all doubts; only remoteness slices all emotions; only grandeur spans all tasks; only principle transforms without fixed form—who under heaven but sages shares such craft!

units.zh: 夫刑而上者謂之道，刑而下者謂之器，化而裁之謂之格。
units.en: Meta-law becomes Dao; applied law becomes instrument; adaptive rules become grids.
units.literal: What transcends punishment is called Way; what lies below punishment is called implement; transforming and trimming it is called normative grid.

units.zh: 刑殺者是冬震曜之象，髡罪者似秋雕落之變，贖失者是春陽悔吝之疵之。
units.en: Capital punishment echoes winter thunder; mutilation echoes autumn decay; fines echo spring faults.
units.literal: Execution resembles winter thunderbolt brilliance; shaved guilt resembles autumn leaf-fall; redeemed fault resembles spring-yang blemishes of regret.

units.zh: 五刑成章，輒相依准，法律之義焉。
units.en: Five chapters interlock by design.
units.literal: Five punishments forming chapters mutually rely—such is law's meaning.

units.zh: 是時侍中盧珽、中書侍郎張華又表：「抄《新律》諸死罪條目，懸之亭傳，以示兆庶。」
units.en: At this time Attendant Lu Ting and Palace Writer Attendant Gentleman Zhang Hua again memorialized: "Copy out the articles for the capital crimes in the New Code and hang them in stations and relay posts to show them to the common people."
units.literal: At this time Attendant Lu Ting and Palace Writer Attendant Gentleman Zhang Hua again memorialized: "Copy out the articles for the capital crimes in the New Code and hang them in stations and relay posts to show them to the common people."

units.zh: 有詔從之。
units.en: The throne agreed.
units.literal: An edict approved.

units.zh: 及劉頌為廷尉，頻表宜復肉刑，不見省，又上言曰：
units.en: Liu Song renewed corporal-punishment petitions from the Ministry of Justice.
units.literal: When Liu Song became commandant of justice he repeatedly memorialized restoring corporal punishment without response; he again spoke:

units.zh: 臣昔上行肉刑，從來積年，遂寢不論。
units.en: Years ago I urged corporal punishment—still tabled.
units.literal: Your servant formerly promoted corporal punishment; years passed yet discussion slept.

units.zh: 臣竊以為議者拘孝文之小仁，而輕違聖王之典刑，未詳之甚，莫過於此。
units.en: Critics indulge Wen's sentimental mercy and forsake classical mutilation.
units.literal: Your servant privately thinks debaters cling to Emperor Wen's petty kindness and lightly violate sage-king canonical punishments—nothing more ignorant.

units.zh: 今死刑重，故非命者眾；
units.en: Heavy capital statutes multiply wrongful deaths;
units.literal: Now capital punishment weighs heavily so unnatural deaths abound;

units.zh: 生刑輕，故罪不禁奸。
units.en: light labor sentences fail to deter wickedness.
units.literal: living punishments weigh lightly so crimes cannot restrain villainy.

units.zh: 所以然者，肉刑不用之所致也。
units.en: Root cause: abandoning corporal options.
units.literal: The reason is failing to use corporal punishments.

units.zh: 今為徒者，類性元惡不軌之族也，去家懸遠，作役山谷，饑寒切身，志不聊生，雖有廉士介者，苟慮不首死，則皆為盜賊，豈況本性奸凶無賴之徒乎！
units.en: Exiled laborers—mostly habitual offenders—starve in mountains until even decent men become thieves.
units.literal: Today labor convicts mostly stem from incorrigible clans; removed far from home toiling in mountains, hunger and cold grip them so life feels unbearable—even honest men, fearing death less than misery, turn bandit—how much more base villains!

units.zh: 又令徒富者輸財，解日歸家，乃無役之人也。
units.en: Rich inmates ransom release while poor ones rot in gangs.
units.literal: Moreover wealthy convicts buy release with property and return home—effectively avoiding labor.

units.zh: 貧者起為奸盜，又不制之虜也。
units.en: Destitute laborers slide into theft without restraint.
units.literal: Poor men rise as robbers-thieves—another unchecked plague.

units.zh: 不刑，則罪無所禁；
units.en: Without mutilation crime spreads unchecked;
units.literal: Without corporal punishment crimes cannot be barred;

units.zh: 不制，則群惡橫肆。
units.en: without deterrence gangs rage openly.
units.literal: without restraint villain packs run rampant.

units.zh: 為法若此，近不盡善也。
units.en: Such policy barely qualifies as sound.
units.literal: Law framed thus hardly reaches perfection.

units.zh: 是以徒亡日屬，賊盜日煩，亡之數者至有十數，得輒加刑，日益一歲，此為終身之徒也。
units.en: Escalating escape penalties trap convicts in perpetual labor.
units.literal: Therefore fugitives multiply daily; theft flourishes; escape counts reach dozens—each capture adds another year until lifetime labor results.

units.zh: 自顧反善無期，而災困逼身，其志亡思盜，勢不得息，事使之然也。
units.en: Hopeless lifers hunt loot because circumstance leaves no choice.
units.literal: Seeing no hope of reform while disaster presses, minds plot theft with no rest—circumstances force it.

units.zh: 古者用刑以止刑，今反於此。
units.en: Ancient law ended crime through punishment; modern practice inverts it.
units.literal: Antiquity used punishments to end punishments—today reverses this.

units.zh: 諸重犯亡者，發過三寸輒重髡之，此以刑生刑；
units.en: Convicts guilty of serious offenses who escape and let their hair grow past three inches are shaved again—punishment spawning punishment;
units.literal: Serious fugitives whose hair grows past three inches receive repeated shaving—punishment breeding punishment;

units.zh: 加作一歲，此以徒生徒也。
units.en: stacked years breed endless labor.
units.literal: adding another year labor produces labor breeding labor.

units.zh: 亡者積多，系囚猥畜。
units.en: Jails overflow with repeat escapees.
units.literal: Escapes accumulate; dungeons swell.

units.zh: 議者曰囚不可不赦，復從而赦之，此為刑不制罪，法不勝奸。
units.en: Endless amnesties admit law cannot defeat crime.
units.literal: Critics say prisoners cannot avoid amnesty—yet amnesty follows—this means punishments cannot master crime and law cannot defeat villainy.

units.zh: 下知法之不勝，相聚而謀為不軌，月異而歲不同。
units.en: Criminals exploit legal weakness with evolving plots.
units.literal: Inferiors knowing law inadequate gather plotting rebellion—monthly shifts yearly alter tactics.

units.zh: 故自頃年以來，奸惡陵暴，所在充斥。
units.en: Recent seasons swarm with violent crime.
units.literal: Thus recent years see villainy bullying truth everywhere.

units.zh: 議者不深思此故，而曰肉刑於名忤聽，忤聽孰與賊盜不禁？
units.en: Cosmetic objection to mutilation ignores rampant robbery.
units.literal: Critics never ponder this yet say corporal punishment offends hearing—which offends more: unpleasant names or unchecked theft?

units.zh: 聖王之制肉刑，遠有深理，其事可得而言，非徒懲其畏剝割之痛而不為也，乃去其為惡之具，使夫奸人無用復肆其志，止奸絕本，理之盡也。
units.en: Mutilation removes criminal capacity, not merely fear.
units.literal: Sage kings devised corporal punishments with profound logic—not merely frightening men from cuts but removing tools of evil so villains cannot resume scheming—cutting roots ends villainy utterly.

units.zh: 亡者刖足，無所用復亡。
units.en: Footless escapees cannot run;
units.literal: Fugitives lose feet—cannot flee again.

units.zh: 盜者截手，無所用復盜。
units.en: handless thieves cannot steal;
units.literal: thieves lose hands—cannot steal again;

units.zh: 淫者割其勢，理亦如之。
units.en: those guilty of illicit sex are castrated on the same reasoning.
units.literal: adulterers lose organs—same reasoning.

units.zh: 除惡塞源，莫善於此，非徒然也。
units.en: Amputation eradicates evil at source.
units.literal: Eliminating evil at its source—nothing superior—no idle gesture.

units.zh: 此等已刑之後，便各歸家，父母妻子，共相養恤，不流離于塗路。
units.en: Maimed offenders stay home supported by kin.
units.literal: After punishment convicts return home—parents, wives, children mutually sustain—not drifting roadside.

units.zh: 有今之困，創愈可役，上准古制，隨宜業作，雖已刑殘，不為虛棄，而所患都塞，又生育繁阜之道自若也。
units.en: Scarred workers still tend fields under supervised labor; society keeps producing.
units.literal: Despite today's hardships wounds heal into usable labor; matching antiquity they take suitable work—though maimed they are not wasted castoffs; worries halt while population still breeds.

units.zh: 今宜取死刑之限輕，及三犯逃亡淫盜，悉以肉刑代之。
units.en: Substitute corporal punishment for the lighter capital cases and for offenders convicted three times of escape, illicit sex, or theft.
units.literal: Now the lighter cases within the range of capital punishment, together with those who have committed escape, illicit sex, or theft three times, should all have corporal punishment substituted for death.

units.zh: 其三歲刑以下，已自杖罰遣，又宜制其罰數，使有常限，不得減此。
units.en: Cap sub-three-year caning with mandatory floors.
units.literal: Punishments three years and below already suffer cane fines—further fix stroke counts with fixed limits never reducible.

units.zh: 其有宜重者，又任之官長。
units.en: Superiors may add weight case by case.
units.literal: When heavier needs arise, local chiefs may adjust.

units.zh: 應四五歲刑者，皆髡笞，笞至一百，稍行，使各有差，悉不復居作。
units.en: Mid felonies become shave-plus-cane without prison labor.
units.literal: Those fit for four- or five-year terms receive shaving plus flogging to one hundred strokes in stages—no more corvée residence.

units.zh: 然後刑不復生刑，徒不復生徒，而殘體為戳，終身作誡。
units.en: Stopping punishment spirals, mutilation educates forever.
units.literal: Then punishment no longer begets punishment nor labor begets labor—maimed bodies stand as lifelong warnings.

units.zh: 人見其痛，畏而不犯，必數倍於今。
units.en: Visible agony deters more than remote labor.
units.literal: People seeing pain fear doubly more than today.

units.zh: 且為惡者隨發被刑，去其為惡之具，此為諸已刑者皆良士也，豈與全其為奸之手足，而蹴居必死之窮地同哉！
units.en: Timely mutilation redeems; intact limbs drive desperados.
units.literal: Evil-doers mutilated on capture lose their tools—such men become good subjects—unlike leaving villain limbs intact to corner them toward death.

units.zh: 而猶曰肉刑不可用，臣竊以為不識務之甚也。
units.en: Denying mutilation misunderstands statecraft.
units.literal: Yet voices say corporal law cannot apply—your servant deems that utter policy blindness.

units.zh: 臣昔常侍左右，數聞明詔，謂肉刑宜用，事便於政。
units.en: When I formerly served as an attendant at your side, I often heard enlightened edicts saying that corporal punishment ought to be used and would benefit government.
units.literal: Your servant once attended the throne often hearing edicts that corporal punishment benefits administration.

units.zh: 願陛下信獨見之斷，使夫能者得奉聖慮，行之於今。
units.en: Trust the policy and commission experts to codify it.
units.literal: May Your Majesty trust this lonely resolve and let able men enact sage worry in our age.

units.zh: 比填溝壑，冀見太平。
units.en: I offer my life to see tranquil rule.
units.literal: I am ready to fill ditches and hope to glimpse great peace.

units.zh: 《周禮》三赦三宥，施於老幼悼耄，黔黎不屬逮者，此非為惡之所出，故刑法逆舍而宥之。
units.en: Rites spare juveniles and senility because guilt rarely originates there.
units.literal: Zhou Rites' three pardons and three mercies cover old young and infirm—commoners not subject to capture—because evil does not stem from them, so law pauses and forgives.

units.zh: 至於自非此族，犯罪則必刑而無赦，此政之理也。
units.en: Anyone outside these exempt groups who commits a crime must be punished without pardon; this is the principle of government.
units.literal: All outside these groups, once guilty, must be punished without mercy—this is governance's pattern.

units.zh: 暨至後世，以時嶮多難，因赦解結，權以行之，又不以寬罪人也。
units.en: Later dynasties amnestied for crisis control, not mercy.
units.literal: Later ages, times treacherous, used amnesties to untie knots—expedient, not true leniency toward culprits.

units.zh: 至今恆以罪積獄繁，赦以散之，是以赦愈數而獄愈塞，如此不已，將至不勝。
units.en: Frequent amnesties stuffed prisons worse.
units.literal: Now crimes pile, jails jam, amnesties scatter them—so more amnesties clog courts—endlessly unsustainable.

units.zh: 原其所由，內刑不用之故也。
units.en: No mutilation forces amnesty bloat.
units.literal: Trace the root—because corporal law lies unused.

units.zh: 今行肉刑，非徒不積，且為惡無具則奸息。
units.en: Mutilation both empties jails and removes criminal means.
units.literal: Enact corporal punishments—not only unclog courts but deprive evil of tools.

units.zh: 去此二端，獄不得繁，故無取於數赦，於政體勝矣。
units.en: With mutilation plus deterrence, amnesties become unnecessary.
units.literal: Remove these two issues—dungeons need not crowd; skip serial amnesties; policy prevails.

units.zh: 疏上，又不見省。
units.en: The throne again shelved Liu Song.
units.literal: Memorial up—again ignored.

units.zh: 至惠帝之世，政出群下，每有疑獄，各立私情，刑法不定，獄訟繁滋。
units.en: Hui's court factionalized justice and docket chaos exploded.
units.literal: By Emperor Hui's reign power scattered below; each doubtful case nursed private bias; punishments wavered; suits multiplied.

units.zh: 尚書裴頠表陳之曰：
units.en: Pei Wei then submitted:
units.literal: Minister Pei Wei memorialized saying:

units.zh: 夫天下之事多塗，非一司之所管；
units.en: State business spans ministries needing division of labor.
units.literal: Affairs under heaven run many paths—not one office may govern all.

units.zh: 中才之情易擾，賴恆制而後定。
units.en: Average officials need fixed rules to stay calm.
units.literal: Middling talents are easily perturbed; they rely on constant systems to settle.

units.zh: 先王知其所以然也，是以辨方分職，為之准局。
units.en: Ancient kings assigned jurisdictions deliberately.
units.literal: Former kings knew this, therefore they divided regions and tasks into measured scopes.

units.zh: 准局既立，各掌其務，刑賞相稱，輕重無二，故下聽有常，群吏安業也。
units.en: Clear jurisdiction balances incentives and steadies clerks.
units.literal: Once scopes stand each manages its charge; reward and punishment match; light and heavy stay even—hence subordinates listen consistently and clerks find peace.

units.zh: 舊宮掖陵廟有水火毀傷之變，然後尚書乃躬自奔赴，其非此也，皆止于郎令史而已。
units.en: Catastrophes alone drew ministers personally; minor roof checks stayed with clerks.
units.literal: Formerly only after palace, tumulus, or temple fire or flood would the Minister himself rush; otherwise only bureau gentlemen handled it.

units.zh: 刑罰所加，各有常刑。
units.en: Each offense had a fixed penalty ladder.
units.literal: Punishment applications each had regular statutes.

units.zh: 去元康四年，大風之後，廟闕屋瓦有數枚傾落，免太常荀寓。
units.en: Yuankang 4 windstorm tiles toppled; Xun Yu took the fall.
units.literal: In fourth year of Yuankang, after great wind, several temple eaves-tiles fell—Minister of Ceremonies Xun Yu was dismissed.

units.zh: 于時以嚴詔所譴，莫敢據正。
units.en: Harsh edicts silenced dissent.
units.literal: At the time harsh edict blame—none dared argue rectitude.

units.zh: 然內外之意，僉謂事輕責重，有違于常。
units.en: Everyone felt penalties disproportionate.
units.literal: Court consensus judged fault light yet punishment heavy—contrary to precedent.

units.zh: 會五年二月有大風，主者懲懼前事。
units.en: Month-two winds next year made clerks paranoid.
units.literal: When fifth year second month brought another gale, officials dreaded repeating prior ordeal.

units.zh: 臣新拜尚書始三日，本曹尚書有疾，權令兼出，按行蘭台。
units.en: I had been appointed Secretary only three days when the Secretary of the responsible bureau fell ill, so I was temporarily ordered to go out in his place and inspect the Orchid Terrace.
units.literal: Your servant had just become Minister three days; chief minister fell ill so your servant temporarily inspected Orchid Terrace.

units.zh: 主者乃瞻望阿棟之間，求索瓦之不正者，得棟上瓦小邪十五處。
units.en: Teams counted fifteen slightly misaligned ridge tiles.
units.literal: Inspectors stared between beams hunting crooked tiles—finding fifteen slightly skewed ridge tiles.

units.zh: 或是始瓦時邪，蓋不足言，風起倉卒，台官更往，太常按行，不及得周，文書未至之頃，便競相禁止。
units.en: Minor skew blamed on builders yet panic triggered blanket bans mid-inspection.
units.literal: Perhaps masons laid them crooked originally—hardly worth mentioning—yet sudden winds sent Terrace officers and Minister of Ceremonies scrambling incomplete inspections while paperwork lagged—everyone raced to embargo repairs.

units.zh: 臣以權兼暫出，出還便罷，不復得窮其事。
units.en: Acting supervisors lost mandate once rotated.
units.literal: Your servant held temporary duty—returning ended authority—could not pursue detail.

units.zh: 而本曹據執，卻問無已。
units.en: Permanent staff kept interrogating Ceremonies.
units.literal: Yet home bureau clung stubbornly questioning endlessly.

units.zh: 臣時具加解遣，而主者畏咎，不從臣言，禁止太常，復興刑獄。
units.en: Despite Pei Wei's orders, terrified clerks prosecuted ritual ministers again.
units.literal: Your servant explained dismissal yet chiefs feared blame—ignored advice—embargoed Minister of Ceremonies reopening trials.

units.zh: 昔漢氏有盜廟玉環者，文帝欲族誅，釋之但處以死刑，曰：「若侵長陵一抔土，何以復加？」
units.en: Formerly, when there was someone under the Han who stole a jade ring from the temple, Emperor Wen wanted to execute his clan, but Zhang Shizhi only sentenced him to death and said, "If he had invaded a handful of soil from Changling, what could be added to this?"
units.literal: Formerly, when there was someone under the Han who stole a jade ring from the temple, Emperor Wen wanted to execute his clan, but Zhang Shizhi only sentenced him to death and said, "If he had invaded a handful of soil from Changling, what could be added to this?"

units.zh: 文帝從之。
units.en: Wendi accepted.
units.literal: Emperor Wen obeyed.

units.zh: 大晉垂制，深惟經遠，山陵不封，園邑不飾，墓而不墳，同乎山壤，是以丘阪存其陳草，使齊乎中原矣。
units.en: Jin tombs lie low without mounds—indistinguishable hills.
units.literal: Great Jin's enduring system reveres distance—imperial tumuli unsealed, park estates unadorned, graves flush with soil like hills—wild grass marks resting kings matching plain earth.

units.zh: 雖陵兆尊嚴，唯毀發然後族之，此古典也。
units.en: Grand Jin reserves clan slaughter for actual tomb breach.
units.literal: Though tombs inspire awe only excavation warrants clan execution—classical rule.

units.zh: 若登踐犯損，失盡敬之道，事止刑罪可也。
units.en: Footprints or careless damage merit regular sentencing only.
units.literal: If treading or bruising loses reverence, ordinary penal guilt suffices.

units.zh: 去八年，奴聽教加誣周龍燒草，廷尉遂奏族龍，一門八口並命。
units.en: Eight years prior a framed Zhou Long nearly lost eight kin.
units.literal: Eight years ago a slave obeying orders falsely accused Zhou Long burning grass—the commandant memorialized clan execution—eight mouths perished.

units.zh: 會龍獄翻，然後得免。
units.en: Retrial freed them.
units.literal: Only when Long's case overturned did they escape.

units.zh: 考之情理，准之前訓，所處實重。
units.en: That verdict exceeded proportional justice.
units.literal: Measured against reason and ancient exempla—the sentence was harsh.

units.zh: 今年八月，陵上荊一枝圍七寸二分者被斫，司徒太常，奔走道路，雖知事小，而案劾難測，搔擾驅馳，各競免負，於今太常禁止未解。
units.en: Petty branch-cutting triggered another Ceremonies inquisition still open.
units.literal: This eighth month someone cut a seven-inch-two-branch vine on the tomb mound—Minister and Ceremonies raced roads knowing matter petty yet unpredictable prosecution harassed everyone avoiding blame—Ceremonies offices remain embargoed.

units.zh: 近日太祝署失火，燒屋三間半。
units.en: Last week the Blessing office fire consumed half the annex.
units.literal: Recently Archivist Directorate fire burned three and a half rooms.

units.zh: 署在廟北，隔道在重牆之內，又即已滅，頻為詔旨所問。
units.en: Fire stayed inside temple walls yet palace demanded endless reports.
units.literal: It sits north of temple inside double walls—already extinguished—yet edicts repeatedly inquire.

units.zh: 主者以詔旨使問頻繁，便責尚書不即案行，輒禁止，尚書免，皆在法外。
units.en: Clerics punished ministers extra-legally for delayed surveys.
units.literal: Handlers, citing frequent edict inquiries, blamed Minister for slow inspection—again embargoed Minister—dismissals landed outside statutory bounds.

units.zh: 刑書之文有限，而舛違之故無方，故有臨時議處之制，誠不能皆得循常也。
units.en: Because written law cannot cover every factual twist, judges need emergency procedures that sometimes break the usual rulebook.
units.literal: Statute text is finite, yet causes of error know no limit—hence the system of ad hoc deliberation; one cannot in every case follow a constant rule.

units.zh: 至於此等，皆為過當，每相逼迫，不得以理，上替聖朝畫一之德，下損崇禮大臣之望。
units.en: These overreactions in tomb cases undercut the court’s commitment to one law for all and embarrass senior ministers who stand for proper ceremony.
units.literal: As for these cases, all have exceeded the proper measure, each side pressing the other, unable to apply reason—above it undermines the sagely court’s virtue of uniform standards, below it injures the expectation that great ministers be honored in ritual.

units.zh: 臣愚以為犯陵上草木，不應乃用同產異刑之制。
units.en: Trampling graveyard growth should not trigger the same draconian kin-punishment statutes used for true desecration.
units.literal: Your servant thinks that treading on plants above an imperial tumulus should not call forth the system of different punishments for those who share the same birth.

units.zh: 按行奏劾，應有定準，相承務重，體例遂虧。
units.en: Inspections and indictments need stable yardsticks, not an ever-harsher drift that warps precedent.
units.literal: Investigations and impeachments ought to have fixed standards; generation after generation they pursued severity, and the body of precedent was thus injured.

units.zh: 或因余事，得容淺深。
units.en: Collateral issues can still adjust how heavy a sentence feels.
units.literal: Sometimes, by way of other matters, one may accommodate lighter or deeper guilt.

units.zh: 頠雖有此表，曲議猶不止。
units.en: Even after Pei Wei’s paper, carping continued.
units.literal: Although Pei had submitted this memorial, captious side-debates still did not cease.

units.zh: 時劉頌為三公尚書，又上疏曰：
units.en: Liu Song, serving as the Three Excellencies’ overseer, then added this argument:
units.literal: At the time Liu Song, as Minister of the Three Dukes, again submitted a memorial saying:

units.zh: 自近世以來，法漸多門，令甚不一。
units.en: Recent decades multiplied alternate legal “doors” and clashing edicts.
units.literal: From recent generations onward, law has gradually acquired many gates, and edicts are extremely inconsistent.

units.zh: 臣今備掌刑斷，職思其憂，謹具啟聞。
units.en: As the minister now holding capital jurisdiction, I must report my concern.
units.literal: Your servant now fully manages criminal decisions; pondering this worry, I respectfully lay it before you.

units.zh: 臣竊伏惟陛下為政，每盡善，故事求曲當，則例不得直；
units.en: Bending every case to feel perfectly tailored breaks consistent rules.
units.literal: Your servant humbly reflects that when Your Majesty governs, every time you seek a perfect match to circumstance; if in precedents and examples you seek a perfect match, the pattern cannot stay straight.

units.zh: 盡善，故法不得全。
units.en: The quest to perfect each outcome shreds a unified code.
units.literal: Because you seek perfection, the law cannot remain whole.

units.zh: 何則？
units.en: Why?
units.literal: Why is that?

units.zh: 夫法者，固以盡理為法，而上求盡善，則諸下牽文就意，以赴主之所許，是以法不得全。
units.en: When clerks stretch clauses to match imperial whim, the statute fractures.
units.literal: Law by its nature takes exhausting principle to be law, but if superiors demand perfection, all subordinates twist the text to match what the ruler likes—therefore the law cannot remain whole.

units.zh: 刑書徵文，徵文必有乖於情聽之斷，而上安于曲當，故執平者因文可引，則生二端。
units.en: Literal argument forks whenever rulers reward clever readings over predictable ones.
units.literal: Criminal writings cite text; citing text necessarily diverges from judgments based on emotional hearings—yet superiors settle for devious fitness, so those who hold balance, wherever text can be stretched, produce paired interpretations.

units.zh: 是法多門，令不一，則吏不知所守，下不知所避。
units.en: A fractured code leaves officials and subjects guessing.
units.literal: Thus law has many gates and edicts do not agree—clerks know not what to guard and commoners know not what to avoid.

units.zh: 奸偽者因法之多門，以售其情，所欲淺深，苟斷不一，則居上者難以檢下，於是事同議異，獄犴不平，有傷於法。
units.en: Sharp lawyers shop forums until punishments become arbitrary.
units.literal: The crafty exploit law’s many gates to peddle their angle; if verdict depth varies at whim, those above cannot inspect those below—same facts spawn divergent opinions and unequal prisons, harming the law.

units.zh: 古人有言：「人主詳，其政荒；
units.en: An ancient said, "When the ruler of men is detailed, his government is desolate;
units.literal: An ancient said, "When the ruler of men is detailed, his government is desolate;

units.zh: 人主期，其事理。」
units.en: when the ruler of men sets terms, his affairs are ordered."
units.literal: when the ruler of men sets terms, his affairs are ordered."

units.zh: 詳匪他，盡善則法傷，故其政荒也。
units.en: Perfectionism corrodes legal uniformity.
units.literal: ‘Meticulous’ means nothing else—seeking perfection injures law, hence government withers.

units.zh: 期者輕重之當，雖不厭情，苟入于文，則循而行之，故其事理也。
units.en: Codified proportionality beats sentimental tailoring.
units.literal: Expectation means fitness of light and heavy; though it may not satisfy hearts, if it enters the text, follow and execute it—therefore affairs become ordered.

units.zh: 夫善用法者，忍違情不厭聽之斷，輕重雖不允人心，經於凡覽，若不可行，法乃得直。
units.en: Sound adjudication accepts unpopular but printed sentences.
units.literal: Those skilled at using law endure violating emotion to preserve consistent hearings; though severity may not please popular hearts, when ordinary review thinks it unenforceable, only then does law stand upright.

units.zh: 又君臣之分，各有所司。
units.en: Sovereign and minister occupy distinct roles.
units.literal: Moreover lord and minister each has his duty.

units.zh: 法欲必奉，故令主者守文；
units.en: Line judges must cling to written clauses.
units.literal: Because law must be obeyed, instruct specialists to guard the text.

units.zh: 理有窮塞，故使大臣釋滯；
units.en: Senior ministers settle statutory deadlocks.
units.literal: Because principle may block, let great ministers release the obstruction.

units.zh: 事有時宜，故人主權斷。
units.en: Only the emperor handles timely exceptions.
units.literal: Because affairs have timely fitness, the human lord wields authority to decide.

units.zh: 主者守文，若釋之執犯蹕之平也；
units.en: Low judges mirror Zhang Shizhi’s refusal to bend the carriage-interdiction rule.
units.literal: Specialists guarding the text resemble Zhang Shizhi holding fast to the impartial verdict on breaking the imperial procession cordon.

units.zh: 大臣釋滯，若公孫弘斷郭解之獄也；
units.en: Senior jurists untangle cases the way Gongsun Hong handled Guo Jie.
units.literal: Great ministers releasing obstruction resemble Gongsun Hong deciding Guo Jie’s prison case.

units.zh: 人主權斷，若漢祖戮丁公之為也。
units.en: Royal discretion recalls Gaozu killing Ding Gong despite merit.
units.literal: Lordly authority deciding resembles Han founder executing Ding Gong’s breach of loyalty.

units.zh: 天下萬事，自非斯格重為，故不近似此類，不得出以意妄議，其餘皆以律令從事。
units.en: In the ten thousand affairs under Heaven, unless they fall under this pattern of weighty action, and unless they are close to similar cases of this kind, one may not bring forth arbitrary deliberations from personal opinion; all the rest must be handled according to statutes and ordinances.
units.literal: In the ten thousand affairs under Heaven, unless they fall under this pattern of weighty action, and unless they are close to similar cases of this kind, one may not bring forth arbitrary deliberations from personal opinion; all the rest must be handled according to statutes and ordinances.

units.zh: 然後法信於下，人聽不惑，吏不容奸，可以言政。
units.en: Predictable law earns trust, foils bribery, and makes governance possible.
units.literal: Only then does law win trust below, popular hearing stays unconfused, clerks cannot harbor deceit, and one may speak of government.

units.zh: 人主軌斯格以責群下，大臣小吏各守其局，則法一矣。
units.en: When ruler and ranks stay inside fixed roles, uniformity returns.
units.literal: The lord uses this pattern to demand performance from all below; great ministers and petty clerks each guard their station—then law is one.

units.zh: 古人有言：「善為政者，看人設教。」
units.en: An ancient said, "Those who are good at government observe the people and establish instruction."
units.literal: An ancient said, "Those who are good at government observe the people and establish instruction."

units.zh: 看人設教，制法之謂也。
units.en: That is how positive law is born.
units.literal: Tailoring teaching to people” means making law.

units.zh: 又曰：「隨時之宜」，當務之謂也。
units.en: “Suit the times” means handling what the moment requires.
units.literal: They also said: ‘Suit the season’s fitness’—that is seizing the present task.

units.zh: 然則看人隨時，在大量也，而制其法。
units.en: People- and time-surveying inform the code’s great design.
units.literal: Therefore watching people and seasons lies in the grand measure, and with that you frame the statutes.

units.zh: 法軌既定則行之，行之信如四時，執之堅如金石，群吏豈得在成制之內，復稱隨時之宜，傍引看人設教，以亂政典哉！
units.en: After promulgation, law must run like clockwork; bureau ranks may not re-open “flexible” teaching to dilute the code.
units.literal: Once the legal track is set, carry it out; its faithfulness is like the four seasons, its firmness like metal and stone—how can host of clerics, within completed systems, again invoke timely fitness, sidelong quote tailored teaching, and disorder the government’s canons!

units.zh: 何則？
units.en: Why not?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 始制之初，固已看人而隨時矣。
units.en: Drafters already embedded people and season into the text.
units.literal: At the first founding, the system already watched people and followed the times.

units.zh: 今若設法未盡當，則宜改之。
units.en: If the code misfits, amend it formally.
units.literal: If the law as set is not yet right, it is right to change it.

units.zh: 若謂已善，不得盡以為制，而使奉用之司公得出入以差輕重也。
units.en: Do not call the code perfect while letting clerks improvise sentence weight.
units.literal: If you say it is already good, you may not take the whole as system yet let implementing offices in and out to shift light and heavy at will.

units.zh: 夫人君所與天下共者，法也。
units.en: Sovereign and realm share the same published law.
units.literal: What the lord shares with all under heaven is the law.

units.zh: 已令四海，不可以不信以為教，方求天下之不慢，不可繩以不信之法。
units.en: Credibility is the foundation of obedience.
units.literal: An edict already commands the four seas—you cannot teach incredibility; seeking not to let the realm despise you, you cannot bind them with untrusted statutes.

units.zh: 且先識有言，人至遇而不可欺也。
units.en: Wise rulers admit plain facts humans cannot fake forever.
units.literal: Moreover earlier wisdom says even clever humans meeting sagacity cannot be deceived.

units.zh: 不謂平時背法意斷，不勝百姓願也。
units.en: Law cannot chase applause case by case.
units.literal: It does not mean ordinarily betraying legal intent in verdicts yet satisfying popular expectation.

units.zh: 上古議事以制，不為刑辟。
units.en: Earliest ages judged case-by-case before codification;
units.literal: High antiquity decided affairs by deliberation, not by carving punishments.

units.zh: 夏殷及周，書法象魏。
units.en: Three dynasties posted statutes on watchtower gates.
units.literal: Xia, Yin, and Zhou hung written law on the signal towers.

units.zh: 三代之君齊聖，然咸棄曲當之妙鑒，而任徵文之直准，非聖有殊，所遇異也。
units.en: Ancient kings preferred predictable text over improvised mercy.
units.literal: Those generations’ lords were uniformly sagely, yet all abandoned ad hoc perfectionism and relied on textual yardsticks—not because sages differed but circumstances did.

units.zh: 今論時敦樸，不及中古，而執平者欲適情之所安，自托於議事以制。
units.en: Today's mediocrity cannot uphold feudal informal justice.
units.literal: Speaking of our age’s honesty, it cannot match middle antiquity, yet balance-holders wish to settle sentiment where convenient, hiding behind deliberative justice.

units.zh: 臣竊以為聽言則美，論理則違。
units.en: Romanticizing discretionary justice contradicts stable governance.
units.literal: Your servant thinks such speech sounds lovely yet violates coherent principle.

units.zh: 然天下至大，事務眾雜，時有不得悉循文如令。
units.en: Mass society produces corner cases beyond codification.
units.literal: Yet the realm is vast and affairs numerous—sometimes one cannot wholly follow text like edicts.

units.zh: 故臣謂宜立格為限，使主者守文，死生以之，不敢錯思于成制之外，以差輕重，則法恆全。
units.en: Publish sentencing grids so clerks cannot freelance aggravation.
units.literal: Therefore your servant proposes erecting grids as limits: specialists guard text; life and death depend on it—they dare not wander imagination beyond settled systems to tweak severity—then law stays constantly whole.

units.zh: 事無正據，名例不及，大臣論當，以釋不滯，則事無閡。
units.en: Senior councils settle gaps statutes omit.
units.literal: When affairs lack direct textual proof and general principles do not reach them, great ministers debate fitness to release blockage—then affairs lack obstruction.

units.zh: 至如非常之斷，出法賞罰，若漢祖戮楚臣之私己，封趙氏之無功，唯人主專之，非奉職之臣所得擬議。
units.en: Extraordinary judgments that reward or punish outside the law, such as the Han founder executing the Chu minister for his own reasons or enfeoffing the meritless Zhao, belong to the ruler alone and are not for officials to propose.
units.literal: As for extraordinary judgments and rewards or punishments outside the law—like the Han founder executing a Chu minister for his own reasons or enfeoffing a Zhao who had no merit—these belong to the ruler alone and are not for serving officials to propose.

units.zh: 然後情求傍請之跡絕，似是而非之奏塞，此蓋齊法之大准也。
units.en: Ending petition warfare restores systemic fairness.
units.literal: Then tracks of emotional lobbying vanish and sophistries resembling truth clog no longer—this aligns law’s grand norms.

units.zh: 主者小吏，處事無常。
units.en: Low clerks oscillate unpredictably.
units.literal: Chief clerks and petty aides discharge affairs without constant rule.

units.zh: 何則？
units.en: Why?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 無情則法徒克，有情則撓法。
units.en: Cold law alienates; sympathetic law corrupts.
units.literal: Without sentiment law merely conquers; with sentiment law bends.

units.zh: 積克似無私，然乃所以得其私，又恆所岨以衛其身。
units.en: Harsh judges cloak selfish safety.
units.literal: Persistent severity seems selfless yet captures private advantage while forever stonewalling self-protection.

units.zh: 斷當恆克，世謂盡公，時一曲法，乃所不疑。
units.en: Callous benches earn praise; mercy invites scrutiny.
units.literal: Verdicts constantly harsh the age calls utterly just; occasional laxity raises no suspicion.

units.zh: 故人君不善倚深似公之斷，而責守文如令之奏，然後得為有檢，此又平法之一端也。
units.en: Rulers must prize textual petitions over performative cruelty.
units.literal: Thus wise lords should not rely on severity posing as fairness yet demand submissions guarding text like edicts—only then may oversight exist—another facet of balanced law.

units.zh: 夫出法權制，指施一事，厭情合聽，可適耳目，誠有臨時當意之快，勝於徵文不允人心也。
units.en: Ad hoc rulings seduce with empathy yet undermine precedent.
units.literal: Extra-statutory authoritative rulings address single incidents, pleasing ears and sentiment—indeed there is momentary satisfaction finer than textual verdicts that fail hearts.

units.zh: 然起為經制，經年施用，恆得一而失十。
units.en: Codifying improvisation yields tiny gains and systemic harm.
units.literal: Yet turning them into standing practice applied year after year usually gains one benefit yet loses ten.

units.zh: 故小有所得者，必大有所失；
units.en: Petty wins precede major losses;
units.literal: Therefore small gain implies large loss;

units.zh: 近有所漏者，必遠有所苞。
units.en: local loopholes widen.
units.literal: near omission implies distant engulfment.

units.zh: 故諳事識體者，善權輕重，不以小害大，不以近妨遠。
units.en: Seasoned jurists weigh systemic harm.
units.literal: Therefore those knowing affairs and grasping forms weigh advantages—never harming the great for the small nor distant for near.

units.zh: 忍曲當之近適，以全簡直之大准。
units.en: Near-term unfairness sometimes preserves long fairness.
units.literal: They tolerate imperfect near fits to preserve broad straightforward norms.

units.zh: 不牽於凡聽之所安，必守徵文以正例。
units.en: Judges anchor doctrine despite applause.
units.literal: They are not dragged by popular comfort yet cling to textual proofs that affirm precedent.

units.zh: 每臨其事，恆禦此心以決斷，此又法之大概也。
units.en: Every bench decision should echo this discipline.
units.literal: Whenever confronting affairs they discipline mind by this rule—again law’s general tenor.

units.zh: 又律法斷罪，皆當以法律令正文，若無正文，依附名例斷之，其正文名例所不及，皆勿論。
units.en: No conviction without positive statute or general-part analogy.
units.literal: Moreover statutes condemning crimes must rely on statute-edict main texts; where main texts lack, attach to general principles; where principles omit matters, do not discuss guilt.

units.zh: 法吏以上，所執不同，得為異議。
units.en: Senior jurists may dispute interpretations.
units.literal: Legal officers and their superiors may submit differing opinions when their interpretations diverge.

units.zh: 如律之文，守法之官，唯當奉用律令。
units.en: Line judges enforce codified law.
units.literal: Per statute text, officers guarding law must reverently apply statutes and edicts.

units.zh: 至於法律之內，所見不同，乃得為異議也。
units.en: Dissent stays intra-statutory.
units.literal: Only differing opinions inside statute-edict texts qualify as dissent.

units.zh: 今限法曹郎令史，意有不同為駁，唯得論釋法律，以正所斷，不得援求諸外，論隨時之宜，以明法官守局之分。
units.en: Dissents cite law books only, never policy memos.
units.literal: Now restrict Director-of-Law gentlemen and clerks: dissent notes must exegete statute alone to straighten verdict—cannot cite outside expedients or seasonal convenience—clarifying jurists’ jurisdictions.

units.zh: 詔下其事。
units.en: The throne circulated Liu Song’s memo.
units.literal: An edict forwarded the matter.

units.zh: 侍中、太宰、汝南王亮奏以為：「夫禮以訓世，而法以整俗，理化之本，事實由之。
units.en: Attendant, Grand Steward, and Prince Liang of Runan submitted that: "Ritual is used to instruct the age, and law is used to order customs. The root of principle and transformation in fact comes from these.
units.literal: Attendant, Grand Steward, and Prince Liang of Runan submitted that: "Ritual is used to instruct the age, and law is used to order customs. The root of principle and transformation in fact comes from these.

units.zh: 若斷不斷，常輕重隨意，則王憲不一，人無所錯矣。
units.en: Inconsistent punishment destroys predictability.
units.literal: If verdicts hesitate and severity swings by whim, royal authority lacks unity and people cannot orient.

units.zh: 故觀人設教，在上之舉；
units.en: Custom policy flows from the throne;
units.literal: Therefore tailoring teaching to people rests with superiors;

units.zh: 守文直法，臣吏之節也。
units.en: judges enforce statutes faithfully.
units.literal: guarding text and law exemplifies ministerial duty.

units.zh: 臣以去太康八年，隨事異議。
units.en: Since Taikang 8 cases wandered off-script.
units.literal: Your servant thinks since Taikang eighth year each matter drew differing opinions.

units.zh: 周懸象魏之書，漢詠畫一之法，誠以法與時共，義不可二。
units.en: Ancient parallels demand singular codes.
units.literal: Zhou hung tower writings; Han praised unified brushstrokes—law must march with time yet principle cannot split.

units.zh: 今法素定，而法為議，則有所開長，以為宜如頌所啟，為永久之制。」
units.en: Now the law has long been fixed, but if the law is made into a matter for deliberation, something will be opened and allowed to grow. We think it fitting to follow what Liu Song has set forth and make it a permanent system."
units.literal: Now the law has long been fixed, but if the law is made into a matter for deliberation, something will be opened and allowed to grow. We think it fitting to follow what Liu Song has set forth and make it a permanent system."

units.zh: 於是門下屬三公曰：「昔先王議事以制，自中古以來，執法斷事，既以立法，誠不宜復求法外小善也。
units.en: Thereupon the Chancellery instructed the Three Excellencies: "Formerly, the former kings deliberated on affairs in order to make regulations. Since middle antiquity, those who held the law and decided affairs, since law had already been established, truly should not again seek small goods outside the law.
units.literal: Thereupon the Chancellery instructed the Three Excellencies: "Formerly, the former kings deliberated on affairs in order to make regulations. Since middle antiquity, those who held the law and decided affairs, since law had already been established, truly should not again seek small goods outside the law.

units.zh: 若常以善奪法，則人逐善而不忌法，其害甚於無法也。
units.en: Mercy metastasizes worse than legal vacuum.
units.literal: If kindness routinely overrides law, people chase kindness without fearing law—harm exceeds having no law.

units.zh: 案啟事，欲令法令斷一，事無二門，郎令史已下，應復出法駁案，隨事以聞也。」
units.en: On examining the submitted matter, we wish to make laws and ordinances decide uniformly, so that affairs have no two gates; from gentlemen clerks and recorders downward, they should again bring out legal refutations of cases and report them according to the affair."
units.literal: On examining the submitted matter, we wish to make laws and ordinances decide uniformly, so that affairs have no two gates; from gentlemen clerks and recorders downward, they should again bring out legal refutations of cases and report them according to the affair."

units.zh: 及于江左，元帝為丞相時，朝廷草創，議斷不循法律，人立異議，高下無狀。
units.en: After the court moved south of the Yangzi, when Emperor Yuan was Chancellor and the court was newly founded, deliberations and judgments did not follow the statutes; each person put forward a different view, without any standard.
units.literal: East of the Yangzi, when Emperor Yuan was Chancellor, court beginnings improvised verdicts outside law—every man voiced dissent; severity lacked measure.

units.zh: 主簿熊遠奏曰：「禮以崇善，法以閑非，故禮有常典，法有常防，人知惡而無邪心。
units.en: Registrar Xiong Yuan memorialized, saying, "Ritual is used to exalt the good, and law is used to restrain wrongdoing; therefore ritual has constant canons, and law has constant defenses, so people know evil and have no perverse mind.
units.literal: Registrar Xiong Yuan memorialized, saying, "Ritual is used to exalt the good, and law is used to restrain wrongdoing; therefore ritual has constant canons, and law has constant defenses, so people know evil and have no perverse mind.

units.zh: 是以周建象魏之制，漢創畫一之法，故能闡弘大道，以至刑厝。
units.en: Tower statutes enabled peaceful ages.
units.literal: Hence Zhou erected tower postings and Han forged unified methods—thus they spread great ways until punishments lay idle.

units.zh: 律令之作，由來尚矣。
units.en: Written law has ancient pedigree.
units.literal: Statutes and edicts emerged long ago.

units.zh: 經賢智，曆夷險，隨時斟酌，最為周備。
units.en: Successive sages polished codes.
units.literal: Sages refined them through difficulty and ease, adapting as needed—most comprehensive.

units.zh: 自軍興以來，法度陵替，至於處事不用律令，競作屬命，人立異議，曲適物情，虧傷大例。
units.en: Warlord adjudication shredded Jin law.
units.literal: Since military emergencies regulations slipped until offices avoided statutes—every house issued commands, every voice differed—twisting sentiment wounded grand norms.

units.zh: 府立節度，復不奉用，臨事改制，朝作夕改，至於主者不敢任法，每輒關咨，委之大官，非為政之體。
units.en: Rotating edicts paralyzed local judges.
units.literal: Headquarters issue directives yet offices ignore them—changing rules morning and evening—clerks dare not apply law, always consulting superiors, abdicating to grandees—not governance style.

units.zh: 若本曹處事不合法令，監司當以法彈違，不得動用開塞，以壞成事。
units.en: Censorates must guard statutory review.
units.literal: If a bureau acts contrary to statute, inspectorates must impeach by law—may not open or block ad hoc to wreck finished cases.

units.zh: 按法蓋粗術，非妙道也，矯割物情，以成法耳。
units.en: Law approximates justice mechanically.
units.literal: Law is coarse craft, not subtle path—it trims sentiment to complete institutions.

units.zh: 若每隨物情，輒改法制，此為以情壞法。
units.en: Sentiment-driven amendment corrupts law.
units.literal: If each time sentiment shifts statutes change, sentiment ruins law.

units.zh: 法之不一，是謂多門，開人事之路，廣私請之端，非先王立法之本意也。
units.en: Multiple legal doors invite corruption.
units.literal: Law’s lack of unity means many gates—opening personal lobbying and widening private requests—not how former kings founded law.

units.zh: 凡為駁議者，若違律令節度，當合經傳及前比故事，不得任情以破成法。
units.en: Appeals require textual authority.
units.literal: All dissenters violating statute procedure must cite classics, precedents, and prior comparators—may not indulge emotion to break settled law.

units.zh: 愚謂宜令錄事更立條制，諸立議者皆當引律令經傳，不得直以情言，無所依准，以虧舊典也。
units.en: Mandate citation standards for memorial debates.
units.literal: Your servant thinks recorders should draft standing rules: debaters must cite statutes and classics—never naked emotion lacking authority—to avoid harming old canons.

units.zh: 若開塞隨宜，權道制物，此是人君之所得行，非臣子所宜專用。
units.en: Only sovereigns wield emergency discretion.
units.literal: If opening or blocking follows convenience—policy tricks manipulating facts—that is what lords may execute, not what subjects monopolize.

units.zh: 主者唯當徵文據法，以事為斷耳。」
units.en: Those in charge should only cite texts, rely on law, and decide according to the affair."
units.literal: Those in charge should only cite texts, rely on law, and decide according to the affair."

units.zh: 是時帝以權宜從事，尚未能從。
units.en: Exigent survival politics delayed reform.
units.literal: At the time the emperor followed expedients and could not yet adopt it.

units.zh: 而河東衛展為晉王大理，考擿故事有不合情者，又上書曰：「今施行詔書，有考子正父死刑，或鞭父母問子所在。
units.en: When Wei Zhan of Hedong was King of Jin's Grand Judge, he examined and picked out precedents that did not accord with human feeling, and again submitted a letter, saying, "Among edicts now being put into effect, some interrogate sons to correct fathers sentenced to death, or whip fathers and mothers to ask where sons are.
units.literal: When Wei Zhan of Hedong was King of Jin's Grand Judge, he examined and picked out precedents that did not accord with human feeling, and again submitted a letter, saying, "Among edicts now being put into effect, some interrogate sons to correct fathers sentenced to death, or whip fathers and mothers to ask where sons are.

units.zh: 近主者所稱《庚寅詔書》，舉家逃亡家長斬。
units.en: The Gengyin order executed fugitive heads of household.
units.literal: Recently handlers cite the Gengyin edict: whole households fleeing mean the household head is beheaded.

units.zh: 若長是逃亡之主，斬之雖重猶可。
units.en: Decapitating actual fugitive elders seems harsh yet logical.
units.literal: If the elder truly leads the flight, beheading—though heavy—is tolerable.

units.zh: 設子孫犯事，將考祖父逃亡，逃亡是子孫，而父祖嬰其酷。
units.en: Pinning flight guilt on grandparents when juniors fled reverses generations.
units.literal: Suppose grandchildren offend yet judges torture grandfathers about flights—the flight belongs to descendants yet ancestors suffer cruelty.

units.zh: 傷順破教，如此者眾。
units.en: Many rulings violate moral order.
units.literal: Such cases wound compliance and break teaching—many exist.

units.zh: 相隱之道離，則君臣之義廢。
units.en: Destroying family silence erodes political loyalty.
units.literal: When mutual concealment splits, lord-minister righteousness perishes.

units.zh: 君臣之義廢，則犯上之奸生矣。
units.en: Broken loyalty breeds rebellion.
units.literal: When lord-minister righteousness perishes, crimes of betraying superiors arise.

units.zh: 秦網密文峻，漢興，掃除煩苛，風移俗易，幾于刑厝。
units.en: Han softened Qin cruelty toward peace.
units.literal: Qin’s net was dense and writing harsh; Han arose sweeping bother—customs shifted until punishments nearly lay idle.

units.zh: 大人革命，不得不蕩其穢匿，通其圮滯。
units.en: Founders purge prior abuses.
units.literal: Great men reforming destiny must scour filth and unblock stagnation.

units.zh: 今詔書宜除者多，有便於當今，著為正條，則法差簡易。」
units.en: Now there are many edicts that should be removed. If those convenient for the present are written as regular articles, the law will be somewhat simpler and easier."
units.literal: Now there are many edicts that should be removed. If those convenient for the present are written as regular articles, the law will be somewhat simpler and easier."

units.zh: 元帝令曰：「禮樂不興，則刑罰不中，是以明罰敕法，先王所慎。
units.en: Emperor Yuan issued an order, saying, "When ritual and music do not flourish, punishments and penalties do not hit the mark. Therefore making punishments clear and ordering laws was something the former kings treated with care.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan issued an order, saying, "When ritual and music do not flourish, punishments and penalties do not hit the mark. Therefore making punishments clear and ordering laws was something the former kings treated with care.

units.zh: 自元康已來，事故薦臻，法禁滋漫。
units.en: Yuankang onward bred proliferating bans.
units.literal: Since Yuankang years incidents multiplied endlessly; prohibitions swelled.

units.zh: 大理所上，宜朝堂會議，蠲除詔書不可用者，此孤所虛心者也。」
units.en: What the Grand Judge has submitted should be deliberated in court; removing edicts that cannot be used is what I await with an open mind."
units.literal: What the Grand Judge has submitted should be deliberated in court; removing edicts that cannot be used is what I await with an open mind."

units.zh: 及帝即位，展為廷尉，又上言：「古者肉刑，事經前聖，漢文除之，增加大辟。
units.en: When the emperor came to the throne, Wei Zhan became Commandant of Justice and again submitted words: "In antiquity, corporal punishments were matters passed through former sages; Emperor Wen of Han abolished them and increased capital penalties.
units.literal: When the emperor came to the throne, Wei Zhan became Commandant of Justice and again submitted words: "In antiquity, corporal punishments were matters passed through former sages; Emperor Wen of Han abolished them and increased capital penalties.

units.zh: 今人戶凋荒，百不遺一，而刑法峻重，非句踐養胎之義也。
units.en: Depopulation clashes with Goujian-style mercy.
units.literal: Now households are devastated—not one in a hundred survives—yet punishments stay harsh—this is not Goujian’s nurture-the-womb kindness.

units.zh: 愚謂宜復古施行，以隆太平之化。」
units.en: I foolishly think it fitting to restore antiquity and put it into effect, in order to exalt the transformation of Great Peace."
units.literal: I foolishly think it fitting to restore antiquity and put it into effect, in order to exalt the transformation of Great Peace."

units.zh: 詔內外通議。
units.en: Court-wide deliberation ensued.
units.literal: Edict ordered inner and outer courts deliberate.

units.zh: 於是驃騎將軍王導、太常賀循、侍中紀瞻、中書郎庾亮、大將軍諮議參軍梅陶、散騎郎張嶷等議，以：「肉刑之典，由來尚矣。
units.en: Thereupon General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao, Chamberlain for Ceremonials He Xun, Attendant Ji Zhan, Palace Writer Gentleman Yu Liang, Great General's Advisory Army Consultant Mei Tao, Cavalier Gentleman Zhang Yi, and others deliberated, saying: "The canon of corporal punishments has long been honored in origin.
